title: 7-round AES-256 impossible-differential key recovery, improved Phan construction

target.description: 7 rounds of standard AES-256 with initial AddRoundKey and final MixColumns omitted. The source reports complete master-key recovery, using impossible-differential subkey elimination followed by key-schedule completion or trial encryption.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures with a varying inverse-shifted column and fixed other bytes; compatible pairs are selected after encryption
assumptions: Uses the four-round impossible differential of Proposition 1 with input/output extension and early rejection of wrong key guesses.

AES-256 cannot use the same 192-bit key-schedule savings. The dedicated row and Section 4.1 give 2^92 data. The conclusion compresses both key-size variants into one sentence; its 2^91.2 is not substituted for the dedicated AES-256 budget.

Section 2's textual AES-256 key-schedule description includes a rotation in the i=4 mod 8 branch; the canonical AES specification has an unrotated SubWord there. This source description discrepancy remains flagged for full-version checking; no alternative cipher is silently substituted.

data.note: Dedicated Table 1 and final Section 4.1 both report 2^92 CP. Section 5 wording says about 2^91.2 for an attack applicable to both AES-192 and AES-256. The dedicated 92 value is retained with this local conflict, not silently replaced by 91.2.

memory.note: No separate memory budget is explicitly supplied for this improved instance/endpoint. Older attack memory figures and other-instance storage are not inherited.

preprocessing.note: Appendix A precomputes and sorts 2^42 candidate pairs into a difference-indexed table. This is a table size/iteration count, not a separately supplied total time in memory-access or full-encryption units.

success.description: The exact impossible relation retains the true hypothesis, and Steps1–6 with Section4.1 include exhaustive full-key completion. The source does not quantify identification of the originally designated master key among keys consistent with the native verification transcript. The earlier conditional1 also required correct original-key validation; that premise is not established merely by exact trial encryptions. Local true-key retention1 remains a separate component. The dedicated AES256 assignment remains2^92 chosen plaintexts and estimated2^163 memory accesses.

review.scope: B76 corrects the B48 derived primary1 after source-first independent review. Complete native enumeration and residual-key search establish inclusion, not a quantified original-key selection law. Expected/variable work is allowed; lack of a hard deadline is not the correction reason. All costs, local components, other conflicts and full-audit gates are preserved.

components.description: PDF6 Proposition1 and the source elimination rule: a true hypothesis cannot satisfy both conditions of the impossible differential and is not discarded by that mathematical contradiction. This is a local retention relation, not a finite-budget uniqueness or residual-search success rate.

PDF6–7: Step2 retains ciphertext pairs with eight designated zero-difference bytes. Source 2^123 candidate pairs become an expected2^59 pairs at the original 2^92-data analysis; the local 64-bit sieve is not a post-reduction survivor count.
